data.gender_notes: Auguste is used as a unisex name in Christian naming traditions.
data.long_meaning: Derived from the Latin word augere, meaning to increase. The name Auguste is of majestic and venerable origin, associated with the Roman god Augus. In Christianity, the name is given to saints and martyrs, reflecting the reverence and respect accorded to them. The name Auguste carries the meaning “Majestic, venerable” and is chosen by families in Christian traditions for the positive qualities it expresses. Linguistically it belongs to the Biblical tradition and is also used in English, Greek, Latin. Parents who choose Auguste usually hope their child will grow to embody majestic, venerable and live with faith, good character and purpose.
data.etymology: Auguste belongs to the Biblical linguistic tradition and is used in Christian naming. Its recorded meaning is “Majestic, venerable.”
data.numerology_meaning: In Pythagorean numerology the letters of Auguste total 4, giving a life-path number of 4. Number 4 is linked with Rahu and with the qualities of stability, discipline and hard work.

in_latin.name: Augusta
in_latin.long_meaning: The name Augusta originates from the Roman title Augustus, meaning great, magnificent. In Christian tradition, it signifies reverence and grandeur, reflecting the Roman Empire's imperial heritage.

in_english.name: Auguste
in_english.long_meaning: The name Auguste is derived from the Latin Augustus, meaning great, magnificent. It has roots in Hebrew and Greek traditions, symbolizing grandeur and spiritual significance. Historically, it was used in the Roman Empire and later adopted in Christian cultures, signifying reverence and nobility.

data.cultural_impact: The name Auguste carries a royal and powerful connotation, especially in the context of the Roman Empire. It was commonly bestowed upon emperors and high-ranking officials, symbolizing the ultimate expression of authority and status. Though the name fell out of favor during the Middle Ages, it gained renewed popularity during the Renaissance and continues to be a significant choice for Christian parents today, signifying strength, dignity, and venerability.
data.spiritual_significance: In the Christian tradition, the name Auguste represents the attributes of faith, courage, and devotion. When given to a child, it is believed to bestow upon them the strength to face challenges with faith, a strong moral character, and a steadfast commitment to their beliefs. Auguste is also associated with the saints and martyrs in Christianity, reflecting their unwavering commitment to their faith in the face of persecution and hardship. Thus, it symbolizes the ultimate triumph of the human spirit over adversity.
data.spiritual_symbolism: Auguste may be derived from the Latin word "augustus," meaning magnificent, majestic, or revered. In a Christian context, the name Auguste could symbolize a person of great inner strength, deep faith, and profound respect for the divine. It may also represent one who inspires awe and admiration, reminding us of the divine presence within us all.
